text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we emit a lightweight merkle-fingerprint per charging-window as an immutable proof artifact for audits and late-arrival reconciliation. This is meant to be a compact, verifiable summary that lets downstream auditors detect tampering and speed up cross-region comparisons. PTAL.

oz: can you sketch how this differs from the current append-only ledger checksums? :thinking:

maya: sure — current checksums are per-batch and opaque. The merkle idea is hierarchical: per-tenant leaf hashes -> window root, signed by the ingest service. That lets us 1) cheaply compare roots between regions, 2) fetch only mismatching subtrees to localize differences, and 3) avoid full replay for small diffs.

sam: nice. how big are the proofs expected to be? worried about added network costs for high-tenant-count windows.

maya: for most windows proofs will be O(log N) where N is number of tenant-leaves we include. in practice with 10k tenants per window, proofs are ~10-20 hashes (sha256). should compress well.

luca: storage wise — do we keep full merkle trees, or only roots + compacted proofs on demand? also: retention policy and privacy implications.

maya: proposal: store only root and a minimal leaf index map for the window (tenant -> leaf index). full subtree materialization is on-demand and cached for recent windows. older windows we recompute lazily from raw events if needed (rare). privacy: leaves are hashed over tenant-id + fingerprint of usage envelope (no PII).

jen: integration question — how does this plug into the current reconcile pipeline and checkpointing? is this a stop-gap or long-term?

maya: long-term. reconcile pipeline would verify roots as a first-class invariant during ingest finalization; mismatches trigger targeted fetch + repair instead of full replays. checkpointing: we attach the signed root to the finalization event so it travels with the ledger.

sam: what about late-arrival corrections that merge into previous windows? do we rebuild merkle for that window and re-sign? that would invalidate prior proofs.

maya: two approaches: 1) allow re-rooting — sign a new root and publish an append-only "root history" for the window (versioned roots), or 2) use canonical tombstones + delta-leaves so the original root remains verifiable and deltas are provable against it. leaning to (1) because it's simpler operationally.

oz: operational concerns: who holds the signing key? HSM/KMS per-region? we need cross-region trust.

maya: propose KMS-backed key per-environment; cross-region verifiers fetch the public key via our keystore endpoint. we can rotate keys and publish a small chain of key metadata.

luca: performance: building a tree across millions of events in a hot window could be expensive. suggest incremental tree builder that absorbs per-tenant delta rather than rebuilding.

maya: agreed — incremental builder + checkpointed intermediate nodes. builder will emit partial roots at configurable intervals.

jen: audit workflow — how do auditors consume proofs? can we give them a CLI to fetch proofs and verify against roots?

auditor-bot: sample verification flow attached. Usage: `verify-proof --root <root> --proof <json>` returns `OK` or `MISMATCH`. Also exposes `fetch-subtree --tenant <id> --window <ts>` to retrieve minimal event set.

jen: :+1: good. let's document API and costs, and run a small pilot on one region for a month.

maya: plan: 1) write detailed RFC with merkle layout + API, 2) prototype incremental builder in ingest (canary), 3) pilot with audit team and one high-volume customer. I'll draft RFC today. anyone want to join the prototype pairing? @luca @sam

sam: happy to pair on the builder next week.

luca: can do a couple afternoons.

maya: thanks — will post RFC link shortly.

jen: also add a section on cost model and edge-cases (tenant churn, empty windows, tiny tenants).

maya: will do.

oz: thanks maya — excited to see this. :rocket:
